newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank of Canada's Thiessen sees stronger Can dollar.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Canada's Thiessen sees stronger Can dollar.

text.p: Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen said on Friday that prospects are good for the Canadian dollar to strengthen over time.
"For cyclical as well as for more fundamental reasons, the prospects are good for a stronger Canadian currency," Thiessen said in a speech to an international foreign exchange convention.

Thiessen told the conference that several analysts as well as the Bank of Canada expect a stronger Canadian dollar in the future and think that the currency is currently undervalued relative to its long-term fundamentals.
The recent weakness in the Canadian dollar was linked in part to Canada's sluggish domestic economic condition, he said.
"As the slack (in the economy) is absorbed, the bank will need to pursue less stimulative monetary conditions, consistent with a durable, low-inflation economic expansion," Thiessen said.
He noted that prospects are good for continued robust expansion in the Canadian economy through 1997 and into 1998, in response to past monetary easing.
With the margin of excess capacity in the economy still fairly wide, Thiessen said, there is ample room for strong growth in coming quarters without a resurgence of inflation.

"Inflation in Canada is stable, at its lowest level in decades. And it has been somewhat below that in the United States since 1992. This implies a potential appreciation of the Canadian dollar vis-a-vis the U.S. dollar over time, if the inflation differential persists."
